question: Do rear feet also leave the ground in one MuJoCo recovery morphology world driven by all 400 recorded V44 walking velocity commands?
telemetry: All outer body poses and twists, joints, all five substep commands, actuator forces, contact points/normals/distances/forces, warnings and exact clocks; no decimation.
initialization: One pre-step generalized-state projection from the first native precommand V44 walking state. Preserve torso world pose/twist and canonical hinge positions/velocities. MuJoCo free-joint angular velocity is local. No settling, height offset, body override, kick, or subsequent initialization. Retain all nine initial body projection errors; constraint slack cannot be imported exactly into a tree.
command_mapping: Retained Godot request -> existing canonical velocity composer with zero residual -> existing MuJoCo host mapping. Godot-to-canonical sign is -1; MuJoCo sign is +1. Restore nonnegative exact integral JSON numbers below 2^53 to integer tokens for Rust's typed integer fields; no rounding, truncation, negative-zero change, or other numeric change. Preserve Godot binary32 motor readbacks separately; replay canonical requested velocities without a new controller call.
model_mapping: Existing public recovery morphology, public selected S169 actuator caps, implicitfast Newton solver, existing five substeps, velocity gain 10 and rotor armature 0.01. Replace only ground plane with the source-sized box (20 by 0.1 by 20 m, top zero) and sliding friction with authored 1.8 on all geoms. Keep existing MuJoCo torsional/rolling friction and contact solver settings. These material and motor responses are not cross-engine calibrated.
contact_timing: Retain production foot-cap classifier on native contact midpoint. Report positive-force support on any substep and the last substep separately; post-integration geometric contacts separately. None is silently equated with Jolt's one-step solved-contact receipt.
coverage_adequacy: One seed without random draws, one fresh child, all 400 source commands and 2000 native steps cover construction/readback, initial-state mapping, the complete recorded hold/release sequence, real fixed-velocity stepping, capture, bounded child lifetime, exact retention and cold no-world result reading. Zero-world tests deny MjModel/MjData and test real compilation/mapping plus crossed-source, owner, limits, timeout, serialization, finalization and no-claim refusals before launch.
